source.title: Leveraging Unlabeled Data to Track Memorization
source.authors: Mahsa Forouzesh; Hanie Sedghi; Patrick Thiran

record.tranche_reason: The study measures how quickly already-trained networks fit newly assigned random labels and relates that resistance to clean test accuracy. It does not train the same recipes on a fully random-label training set and measure held-out accuracy.
record.gate_note: The reported random-label resistance results bear on the claim's subject, but do not test the stated versions: the study does not test whether the same recipes both fit random labels nearly perfectly and generalize on natural labels, or the listed architecture, optimizer, batch-size, regularization, size, sharpness, or example-removal claims.
record.test_reason: The study measures resistance to fitting newly assigned incorrect labels and evaluates a memorization metric and model-selection method. These are related to generalization, but none tests V1–V8. In particular, fitting one relabeled sample after pretraining does not establish V1's coexistence of full random-label fitting and natural-label generalization under the same recipe.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate but incomplete. The authors conclude that higher-test-accuracy models resist fitting a randomly labeled set, that susceptibility tracks noisy-label memorization, and that susceptibility together with overall training accuracy can select models that generalize well without access to ground-truth training labels.
record.recipe_differences: The study measures resistance to a new randomly labeled sample after pretraining on clean or noisy labels; it does not train on random labels as the primary task and test on held-out examples.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported resistance varies with the pretrained model's test accuracy and whether the new sample is incorrectly or correctly labeled. The single correctly labeled sample comparison is described in Figure 14, but no numeric step result is stated in the supplied text.

fits_no_version.finding: The clean-trained GoogLeNet with 95.36% initial test accuracy fits a single incorrect label after 99 steps; the noise-trained checkpoint with 58.35% initial test accuracy does so after 2 steps.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: For these pretrained CIFAR-10 checkpoints, higher clean test accuracy accompanies greater resistance to fitting a newly assigned incorrect label.

fits_no_version.finding: Susceptibility correlates with accuracy on incorrectly labeled training examples; Figure 3 reports Pearson correlation 0.884 on CIFAR-10 with 50% label noise.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Loss reduction after an update on randomly labeled data can track noisy-label fitting across the tested models and checkpoints.

record.problems: The directly stated step-count comparison uses one sample and two pretrained checkpoints. The reported resistance result is narrower than the claim's random-label training and held-out generalization comparison.
record.rows_left_out: No additional numeric step results are stated in the supplied text for the Figure 13 examples; the caption contains wording inconsistent with the paper's stated pattern, so those examples were not extracted as result rows.

untested.parts: Matched recipes fitting a fully random-label dataset nearly perfectly, generalizing on natural labels, and remaining at chance on held-out random labels.
Natural-label test error as width increases beyond the zero-training-error threshold. Figure 28 instead relates width configurations to noisy-label fitting and susceptibility.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and the contribution of local connectivity.
Held-out performance comparisons between adaptive optimizers and SGD under specified tuning budgets. Including both optimizers does not supply this comparison.
Training batch-size effects on held-out performance under fixed epoch budgets. Figure 34 varies the susceptibility evaluation set size.
Dropout's effect on held-out error across data sizes and regularization settings.
Magnitude-aware weight sharpness and its ranking of generalization gaps relative to norm and margin measures. Susceptibility measures loss change after an optimization step.
Removing examples selected by inclusion-based label memorization, retraining, and comparing test accuracy with equal-sized random removals.

record.verdict_notes: No verdicts apply because no listed version is tested. The additional model-selection results evaluate the study's method. Figures 13 and 15 contain caption wording opposite to the surrounding prose about resistance; this does not affect the explicitly stated Figure 2 step counts.

versions.untested_parts: Does not train the same architectures and recipes to fit random labels nearly perfectly and then compare held-out accuracy on random versus natural labels.
Does not sweep width past the zero-training-error threshold and measure natural-label test error.
Does not compare convolutional and fully connected networks on natural-label image generalization.
Does not compare adaptive optimizers with SGD on held-out performance under the stated tuning conditions.
Does not test large-batch generalization gaps under fixed epoch budgets.
Does not test dropout's effect on held-out error.
Does not measure magnitude-aware sharpness or compare it with norm- and margin-based gap measures.
Does not remove memorized examples and retrain to measure the resulting change in test accuracy.

rows.subject: Network1 (GoogLeNet)
rows.stage_stated: pre-trained on CIFAR-10 dataset with clean labels
rows.operation_detail: Trained on one incorrectly randomly labeled sample; report gives steps until the sample is memorized.

conditions.value: single sample with assigned label “cat” and ground-truth label “deer”

rows.measure: Steps to memorize the incorrectly labeled sample
rows.note: The paper reports initial test accuracy 95.36%; this measures resistance of a pretrained model to one new incorrect label, not random-label training and held-out accuracy.
rows.check: The 99-step value and model identification are correct, but the measure cannot determine any listed version. Appendix B specifies that the relabeled sample comes from the training set; it is not a previously unseen input. Pretraining also uses weight decay.

rows.measure: Steps to memorize the incorrectly labeled sample
